scope.source: final-sequence 60-second three-camera run; SESSION_CONFIG.json is authoritative for typed settings
scope.instrumentation: bounded in-memory aggregates, one terminal JSONL summary per owner; no per-frame disk logging

eye_tracking.note: 100 Hz is typed device setting; observed trigger/queue rate was approximately 60 Hz and used for queue sizing.

queue_capacity_assessment.engineering_heuristic: ceil(max_consumer_service_seconds * measured_enqueue_rate_per_second * 1.2); separate comparison ceil(max_waiting_pixels * 1.2). This is a one-run sizing heuristic, not a guarantee.
queue_capacity_assessment.assessment: Retain capacity 17 for the next bounded experiment: it covers all measured 20%-margin heuristics, all queues drained with zero capacity drops, and eye tracking is exactly at the service-rate heuristic bound. Do not increase to 26 from these data alone. This does not establish sustained worst-case headroom; eye receipt-to-enqueue reached 33.996 ms and service maxima exceed a single 60 Hz frame period, so monitor repeat runs and sustained occupancy. A counterfactual 100 Hz eye arrival assumption would imply capacity 28 under the same service heuristic, but does not match the externally triggered observed session rate.

camera_terminal_delivery.comparison_rule: Compare last valid retrieve return to trial cutoff and terminal-start separately; A10 drain allowance is exposure + transfer + one frame period after external OFF terminal outcome. The 125 ms configured allowance is not evidence that the complete A10-derived margin was consumed.
camera_terminal_delivery.interpretation: Behavioral camera returned one additional valid result after terminal start. Tracking and eye had no valid retrieve after terminal start; their last valid frames occurred 14.8 ms and 14.6 ms before terminal start. Stop-capture elapsed time includes configured wait and is not delivery-tail demand. Last-valid-after-cutoff tails were 64.9687 ms (behavioral), 33.8564 ms (tracking), and 34.1135 ms (eye); all are below the configured 125 ms cutoff-relative window. A10 measures drain margin after external OFF reaches terminal outcome, so cutoff-relative remainder is not proof of unused A10 margin. The behavioral tail exceeded exposure plus one nominal frame period by 6.6 ms; external OFF timing and transfer components are not independently decomposed here.

file_sync_cadence.assessment: All measured successful-sync intervals were below 1.2 seconds after the cadence correction; all reported close operations returned. Maximum interval was behavioral video at 1040.5247 ms. These are observed maxima for this run, not long-term guarantees.

lifecycle_client_timing.status: No serial lifecycle client report timestamps for trial Start/Stop were present in the run evidence; run.json operation timings cover configuration/setup/session operations but not trial lifecycle reports.
lifecycle_client_timing.note: Do not infer client report latency/headroom from camera terminal or file-close timestamps.

limitations: Single 60-second trial; final sequence temporarily enabled eye tracking and was restored afterward.
Queue maxima are single-run observations. Metrics called max_waiting_pixels and max_pending_records are not interchangeable with a formal worst-case queue bound.
No source revision/hash or full independent media decode is recorded in this assessment.
Timing instrumentation adds bounded in-memory counter/timestamp work; no per-frame disk I/O.

visual_stimulus_admission.interpretation: The 3,078 admission capacity drops are distinct from CFR duplicate output frames (3,098) and same-slot omissions (6). This is visual-stimulus admission pressure, not a camera RecordingQueue drop. The capture-slot cap was fully occupied; this evidence does not justify changing camera queue capacity.
